extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature — scientists, academics, and technical professionals (early 20th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used in reviewing scientific monographs and practical manuals (chemistry/resins) and procedural requirements appearing in related academic/job notices. Covers expectations about experimental rigour, nomenclature, material authenticity, documentation, and practical presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of purity before naming substances
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assign names and formulae to amorphous or ill-defined products unless there are adequate constants/criteria to regard them as pure definite substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer objects to treating amorphous products (which often lack constants that may be regarded as criteria of purity) as definite substances simply because they have been isolated and analysed; naming and formulae assigned without sufficient proof risk propagating uncertain entries into the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive identification of new substances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a substance resembling a known compound is encountered, the investigator must ascertain definitely whether the two substances are identical before proposing a new denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic notes the improper practice of assuming probable distinctness and coining names by attaching descriptive prefixes (e.g., variants of abietic acid) without conclusive identity tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct and non-misleading chemical nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Use chemical terminology that accurately reflects functional groups and composition; avoid terms whose suffixes imply functional groups not present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the term 'resinolic acid' would imply a hydroxyl plus a carboxyl; '-ene' generally implies a hydrocarbon — applying such endings to substances that do not possess the implied groups is objectionable and misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide authentic botanical material and habitat information
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure and report authentic plant material and habitat data when studying plant-derived substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer praises the author's care in obtaining authentic material during travels and emphasizes the value of botanical and habitat information as an essential part of monographs on vegetable products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness and scope of monograph coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A monograph should aim to cover the field broadly and include the important classes of products; minor omissions may be acceptable but significant gaps reduce utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some resinous products escaped notice, such omissions are tolerable if they are of little importance; overall completeness is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide useful apparatus/contents aids (contents list and index)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a full contents list and, preferably, a comprehensive index to enhance the book's usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer notes that while a fairly full contents list is given, the book would have been more useful with a comprehensive index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and practicality in descriptions for practical manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: For books intended for practitioners, descriptions of processes and plant/industrial apparatus should be lucid and practical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Schweizer's book, aimed at the 'practical man,' is valued for lucid process descriptions and clear illustrations of distilling and other apparatus (some from the author's designs). Such practical clarity enhances the work's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of illustrations and printed material
rubrics_metrics.description: Well‑printed illustrations and clear printing improve the value and accessibility of technical descriptions and apparatus drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations of apparatus and well-printed figures are specifically praised as enhancing the usefulness of practical chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid typographical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain typographical accuracy throughout the work; frequent misprints undermine clarity and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer points to a clear misprint ('position' for 'composition') and a considerable number of slips, implying these detract from the book's quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include economic/industrial relevance where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the economic importance and industrial uses of products (e.g., latices, resins, rubbers) when relevant to the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer highlights the section on latices and products obtained from them as of great economic importance at the present moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of ability to conduct independent research (research fellowship applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must give evidence of ability to conduct independent research, state the nature of intended research, and provide particulars of previous training and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Marling Research Fellowship, candidates should, if possible, state the research they intend to pursue under the professor's direction and provide details of prior training; there is a deadline for applications and details obtainable from the registrar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and experience for school science posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for school science teaching posts should possess a degree or equivalent and relevant experience; practical laboratory care skills and specialist subject competence are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A 'Science Mistress' is required to teach Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics and care for laboratories; degree or equivalent and experience are essential and training preferred. Salary varies with qualifications and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and documentary requirements for scientific posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for technical or instructional posts must submit testimonials, specimens of work (where relevant), and apply by specified deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queen's College assistant post requires enclosing copies of testimonials and specimens of drawings; Assistant Bacteriologist must send two recent testimonials before the deadline; other posts specify application procedure (stamped addressed envelope, last dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional job duties and salary tied to qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Job adverts define specific duties (e.g., teaching subjects, laboratory supervision, diagnostic work) and link salary ranges to qualifications and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Assistant Bacteriologist (examination of waters/sewages, disease diagnosis, salary £150), Queen's College assistant (salary from £135 to £150 according to qualifications), and Woolwich Polytechnic lecturer with salary and annual increments; duties commence on specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical apparatus description should include durability and maintenance claims with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming improved apparatus performance (e.g., lasting many months without renewals or requiring less maintenance), provide users' reports or evidence to support such claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer quotes a practitioner: apparatus 'easily works for six months without cleaning'; such empirical claims should be documented; also note on material savings when apparatus lasts long in frequent use.
